content.intro: This lesson covers Introduction to Office Scripts as part of Office Scripts and Power Automate. It follows the attached Excel curriculum, with an emphasis on small examples and verification.
content.why_it_matters: Introduction to Office Scripts contributes to reliable business reporting and professional spreadsheet delivery. Document assumptions, verify results independently, and separate optional platform tools from core Excel behavior. Compatibility: Office Scripts and Power Automate require a supported Microsoft 365 environment and tenant configuration. Do not assume a desktop macro or a browser-hosted script will be available on every account.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Introduction to Office Scripts focuses on the following parts of the supplied syllabus: Office Scripts use cases; Recording and writing scripts; Script editor; Differences between scripts and VBA. Keep the underlying source data visible and make each assumption explicit.

content_blocks.code:
Sub AddReportTimestamp()
    Range("B1").Value = Now
End Sub
content_blocks.expected_output: Writes the current date/time into cell B1 in the active worksheet. Test on a copy of a workbook; the macro was not executed by CodeLeaf.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run only inside desktop Excel’s VBA editor on a non-sensitive copy of a workbook. Save as .xlsm only if the macro must be retained; use trusted code and inspect permissions.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a small, known dataset for introduction to office scripts. Apply the example above, compute or inspect at least one result independently, then deliberately try a blank, duplicate, boundary, or not-found case where relevant.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates introduction to office scripts. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. Where the concept requires a specialized Excel feature, first verify that feature is available in your Excel edition.

content.task: Build or inspect an Excel example that demonstrates introduction to office scripts; use the example to verify one normal and one edge case, and write down any version or tool dependency.
task_acceptance_criteria: The worksheet/workflow uses a clear, labeled source range and explicit assumptions.
The learner records an expected output and independently compares it with the actual result.
At least one relevant edge case is checked; data and formula errors are not silently concealed.
The workbook is saved as a copy and compatibility/security/accessibility notes are followed where relevant.
hints: Reduce the problem to a small range with known values before scaling it up.
Inspect cell values and formulas, not only displayed formatting; verify data types, references and range boundaries.
Compare expected versus actual results and check the Microsoft documentation for version-specific functions or tools.
content.expected_output: Writes the current date/time into cell B1 in the active worksheet. Test on a copy of a workbook; the macro was not executed by CodeLeaf.
common_mistakes: Assuming the displayed format is the same as the stored value or data type.
Using an incorrect range boundary, a mismatched lookup key, or an unverified assumption.
Trusting a result without comparing it with a known calculation or checking a failure/edge case.
summary: Introduction to Office Scripts supports the workflow in Office Scripts and Power Automate.
Use a small example, make assumptions visible, and verify the result against the source.
Check target-version availability and keep a clean copy before making high-impact changes.
